title: Deep in-the-money LEAPS instead of shares for core holdings
summary: For core holdings the speaker buys deep in-the-money LEAPS instead of shares. On Broadcom near $400 he chose the $200 strike for a 96 delta, at just over $200: about half the capital. The unused cash earns interest and is dry powder. Costs: a small time premium (a financing cost), no dividends, and an expiration to manage.

steps.caption: Broadcom trades near $400. 100 shares cost about $40,000.
Shares: full upside, full downside, all capital tied up.
The $200 strike LEAPS has about a 96 delta and costs just over $200: about half the capital.
The lines track closely above the strike. The small gap is the time premium, a financing cost.
Breakeven is the strike plus the premium, slightly above today's price.
The other half of the capital stays in cash, earns interest and acts as dry powder.

takeaways: A deep ITM LEAPS gives stock-like exposure for about half the capital.
Cash not used earns interest and is dry powder for selloffs; options are not margined.
The time premium is a financing cost that the interest roughly offsets.
Calls pay no dividends and expire, so they need management.
caveats: The speaker says this is not a trade recommendation. AVGO is not in the backtest universe, so the preset uses other large caps.
Holding a single name with LEAPS can exceed the owner's LEAPS cap; size by exposure.
Tax treatment depends on your situation.

backtest.note: About 95 delta LEAPS, 15 months out, rolled with about 3 months left, as a stock replacement.
